### Don't Idolize the Past
Author: Alistair Begg
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/truth-for-life/truth-for-life-august-11-2017.html
Passage: Job 29:2
Points:
- Believers often look back wistfully on past seasons of spiritual intimacy while enduring present gloom and dryness.
- Spiritual decline frequently stems from neglected private prayer, worldly affections, or subtle self-righteous pride.
- Merely sighing over lost spiritual joy accomplishes nothing and leaves the heart dissatisfied.
- Christians should return directly to Christ in humble prayer, trusting His grace to restore fellowship and light.

### When My Church Was Washed with Butter
Author: Benjamin Vrbicek
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/when-church-washed-butter/
Passage: Job 29:2, 6
Points:
- Longing for previous seasons of joy and ease reflects Job’s righteous grief over lost blessings.
- Job mourned not mere luxury, but active ministry to others, family communion, and the felt favor of God.
- Hard seasons expose self-reliance and dismantle subtle idols tied to identity and successful work.
- God's sustaining presence remains just as real during times in the ashes as in days of abundance.
